stem: What does a drug's elimination half-life describe?

options.A: The approximate time required for the amount or concentration of drug in the body to decrease by 50%
options.B: The time required for every molecule of drug to leave the body completely
options.C: The time until a medication reaches its expiration date
options.D: The interval between manufacturing and dispensing

rationale: Elimination half-life is the time required for the amount or concentration of a drug in the body to decline by approximately one-half during elimination.
educational_objective: Define elimination half-life in clinically relevant pharmacokinetic terms.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf (StatPearls)
source_locator: Elimination half-life definition: time required for plasma concentration/amount to decrease by 50%
source_claim_supported: Drug half-life is the time required for the amount/concentration to fall by approximately 50%.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12/PDF p.16
correction_summary: Rewrote the definition to the standard 50% elimination concept and removed wording implying complete drug disappearance.
